label: EU(7)-PIM: ferrous sulfate above 325 mg a day
title: Ferrous sulfate above 325 mg a day in an older person
statement: Iron supplements / Ferrous sulfate (>325 mg/d) | In lists: 6 (B) | Main reason: Doses >325 mg/d do not considerably increase the amount absorbed but greatly increase the incidence of constipation | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Intravenous iron E

plain_summary: Taking more than 325 mg of ferrous sulfate a day adds little to the iron the body absorbs and makes constipation much more likely. Ask how many tablets, capsules or millilitres the patient takes each day, whether they take any other iron bought without a prescription, and whether they have constipation.

medicine_groups.name: Ferrous sulfate taken by mouth
medicine_groups.note: Ferro-Gradumet, Ferro-grad and Ferrogen tablets each hold 325 mg of ferrous sulfate. Ferro-Grad C, Ferrogen Iron plus Vitamin C, Ferro-Max C, Ferrovance C, Ferro plus Vit C and Iron plus C tablets each hold 325 mg of ferrous sulfate with vitamin C. Ferro-Grad F and FGF tablets each hold 250 mg with folic acid. Fefol capsules each hold 270 mg with folic acid. Ferro-Liquid holds 30 mg of ferrous sulfate in each mL. Ferrous sulfate may be shown as dried ferrous sulfate. Other iron salts, such as ferrous fumarate (Ferro-Tab) and iron polymaltose (Maltofer), are not judged by this limit. Iron given by injection or infusion does not count, and multivitamins that hold a little iron do not count.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when the directions for a Group A medicine (ferrous sulfate taken by mouth) give more than 325 mg of ferrous sulfate a day to a person with a recorded age of 65 or older. If age is missing and the medicine pattern matches, report only a possible finding and ask for the patient’s age. An age below 65 does not meet this criterion. Work out the daily dose as the ferrous sulfate strength of one tablet, capsule or mL multiplied by the number taken each day, for example ONE 325 mg tablet twice a day is 650 mg a day. Exactly 325 mg a day or less is not a finding, and one supply at the higher dose is enough. If the daily amount is unclear or a range includes doses both at or below and above 325 mg, report only a possible finding and ask how much the patient takes each day. If the lowest stated daily dose exceeds 325 mg, the dose condition is met. A range wholly at or below 325 mg does not qualify. Apply the age rule in each case.
cannot_be_seen: Why iron was started, the haemoglobin and iron study results, and whether the patient has constipation. Also how many tablets are really taken each day, iron bought without a prescription, and medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether more than 325 mg of ferrous sulfate a day is still needed, and whether the patient has constipation.
